Simulate Method Comparison Data

Source: R/sim_methods.R
sim_methods.Rd

Simulates measurements of a set of items by several methods, with or without replicates, from the variance component model of Carstensen (2010) with a linear (scaled) relation between methods. Useful for planning studies, checking methods by simulation, and examples.

Usage

sim_methods(
  n_items = 50,
  n_reps = 1,
  methods = c("A", "B"),
  alpha = 0,
  beta = 1,
  mu_mean = 0,
  mu_sd = 1,
  tau = 0,
  omega = 0,
  sigma = 1,
  replicates = c("exchangeable", "linked"),
  p_missing = 0,
  transform = "none",
  seed = NULL,
  mu_values = NULL
)

Arguments

n_items

Number of items (subjects).

n_reps

Number of replicate measurements of each item by each method (before any are removed by p_missing).

methods

Character vector of method names (at least two). The first is the reference method.

alpha, beta

Intercepts and slopes of each method on the common item scale (see details). Scalars are recycled to length(methods).

mu_mean, mu_sd

Mean and SD of the true item values mu_i, which are drawn from a normal distribution.

tau

SD of the method-by-item interaction c_mi on the item scale. A scalar (common) or one value per method.

omega

SD of the item-by-replicate effect a_ir (common to all methods, on the item scale). Only used when replicates = "linked".

sigma

Residual (measurement error) SD of each method, on that method's scale. A scalar or one value per method.

replicates

"exchangeable" (default) or "linked". With linked replicates, all methods measure an item on the same occasions, which share the effect a_ir.

p_missing

Probability that each measurement is removed at random. At least one measurement of each item by each method is kept.

transform

Transformation (see method_vc()). If not "none", the data are simulated on the transformed scale and back-transformed, so all parameters refer to the transformed scale.

seed

Optional seed. The global random number generator state is restored afterwards.

mu_values

Optional numeric vector of length n_items with fixed true item values mu_i, used instead of drawing them (mu_mean and mu_sd are then ignored). Used for the parametric bootstrap in method_convert().

Value

A tibble with columns id, method (a factor, levels in the order of methods), repl, and y, with attribute truth (see details).

Details

Measurement r of item i by method m is $$y_{mir} = \alpha_m + \beta_m (\mu_i + a_{ir} + c_{mi}) + e_{mir},$$ with \(\mu_i \sim N(\mu, \sigma_\mu^2)\), \(a_{ir} \sim N(0, \omega^2)\) (linked replicates only), \(c_{mi} \sim N(0, \tau_m^2)\), and \(e_{mir} \sim N(0, \sigma_m^2)\) (Carstensen, 2010, eq. 7.1). With all \(\beta_m = 1\), this is the constant bias model (eq. 5.1/5.2) used by method_vc().

The truth attribute holds the parameters and the quantities derived from them, on the (transformed) analysis scale:

  • params: the parameters, one row per method, with the y-scale SDs tau_y (\(\beta_m \tau_m\)) and omega_y (\(\beta_m \omega\)).

  • pairs: for each pair of methods (method1 - method2), the bias at mu_mean, the SD of the difference between single measurements of the same item (on the same occasion, for linked replicates), and the corresponding 95% limits of agreement. The bias is constant over items only when the slopes are equal (constant_bias).

  • repeatability: for each method, sigma, the 95% repeatability coefficient \(1.96 \sqrt{2} \sigma_m\), and, for linked replicates, the reproducibility coefficient \(1.96 \sqrt{2} \sqrt{\sigma_m^2 + \beta_m^2 \omega^2}\).

  • conversion: for each ordered pair (to, from), the conversion intercept, slope, and prediction SD (Carstensen, 2010, section 7.1).

References

Carstensen, B. (2010). Comparing Clinical Measurement Methods: A Practical Guide. Wiley.

See also

method_vc(), method_convert(), mc_long()

Examples

# three methods, linked replicates, constant bias
dat = sim_methods(n_items = 30, n_reps = 3, methods = c("A", "B", "C"),
                  alpha = c(0, 0.5, -0.2), tau = 0.3, omega = 0.4,
                  sigma = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.4), replicates = "linked",
                  seed = 1)
head(dat)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>      id method  repl      y
#>   <int> <fct>  <int>  <dbl>
#> 1     1 A          1 -0.284
#> 2     1 A          2 -0.229
#> 3     1 A          3 -1.09 
#> 4     1 B          1  1.03 
#> 5     1 B          2  1.73 
#> 6     1 B          3 -0.567
attr(dat, "truth")$pairs
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   method1 method2  bias    sd lower_loa upper_loa constant_bias
#>   <chr>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <lgl>        
#> 1 A       B        -0.5 0.721    -1.91      0.913 TRUE         
#> 2 A       C         0.2 0.656    -1.09      1.49  TRUE         
#> 3 B       C         0.7 0.768    -0.805     2.21  TRUE
